subject: Meteorology
title: Post-Tropical Transition
description: A quick win: understand Post-Tropical Transition.

hook.text: When a tropical cyclone moves over cool water, it transforms—losing its warm core but not necessarily its danger.

buildup.text: As it interacts with midlatitude fronts, it becomes extratropical—driven by temperature contrasts instead of warm ocean.

discovery.text: Post-tropical storms can actually grow larger—their wind field expands even as maximum winds decrease.

twist.text: Superstorm Sandy went post-tropical just before hitting New Jersey—but its huge size amplified the devastating surge.

climax.text: Europe regularly receives the remnants of Atlantic hurricanes—they arrive as powerful windstorms from the west.

punchline.text: Losing 'tropical' status doesn't mean losing potency.
